items.title: Jimmy Owens — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The music that my father played most of the time were people like Duke Ellington, Billie Holliday... this is what I was hearing when I was a kid.

ctx.x: When you were a child, did you hear jazz in the house?

Oh yes, my father played jazz all the time on the record player, Victrola. When I was three or four years old, I had my favorite records that I could go and pick out the record and put it on the Victrola and play it. The music that my father played most of the time were people like Duke Ellington, Billie Holliday, Count Basie’s band, Charlie Shavers, this is what I was hearing when I was a kid.
Do you remember the first live jazz that you heard?

items.title: Jimmy Owens interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: Being Billie Holiday, being Bessie Smith and Louis Armstrong. There were no hotels, there were no places to eat.

ctx.x: live. There was music all the time records. And my father would pick me up when I was three and four years old, we had a huge mirror in our living room, and he’d pick me up and dance with me to Stumpy Jones or a Billie Holiday record or an Art Tatum record. And I used to love to see myself in the mirror you know. And I guess this is what put the sound of the music in my ear. At, I think he told me I was four years old, he could tell me, “Jimmy, go play your favorite record.” And I’d go among all the records and…

That’s great. Did the musicians that you met, either as teachers or just in the clubs, did you get a sense of them instilling you with other things, just besides the playing of the music? © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
